name: ARN Smart AI-Powered Visitor Intent
author: arnsmart

sections.description:
Most visitors leave without saying what they were looking for. ARN Smart AI-Powered Visitor Intent asks them: a light sticky bar opens a short panel where visitors pick their reason for visiting, leave their contact details if they want, or reach you directly by Call, Email or WhatsApp.

Display rules and triggers decide where and when the panel appears. Analytics show views, responses, contact clicks and the intent mix, and optional AI insights (your own API key) turn the numbers into plain recommendations. Without AI, built-in rule-based insights still work.

✨ Why Visitor Intent?

  • Ask instead of guess – visitors tell you in one click why they came; contact details are optional.
  • Works right after activation – the homepage bar starts with sample texts you can replace under Visitor Intent → Settings.
  • One plugin for intent, leads and contact – panel, contact form, contact widget, notifications and analytics share one settings screen.
  • Loads only where it shows – scripts load only where the display rules or the recommendations block need them.
  • Your data stays on your site – responses stay in WordPress, visible only to administrators; no ARN server, no license key.
  • AI is optional – off by default and uses your own provider key; every chart and summary works without it.

🎯 Visitor intent capture and lead generation

  • Bar and panel: primary and action texts on the bar at the bottom of the page; title, introduction and optional note in the panel. Visitors can close the panel or dismiss the bar.
  • Intent question and reasons: one reason per line; only configured reasons are accepted.
  • Optional contact form: “leave my contact details” or “submit anonymously”; Full Name, Company, Email, LinkedIn and Message each have an on/off switch, label, placeholder and required setting.
  • Editable texts: contact question, Yes and No options, submit button, success title and message.
  • Appearance: bar background, text, accent and panel colors, minimum bar height, panel content width, field and button radius, animation speed (fast, normal, slow) and shadow strength.
  • No page reload, no spam: honeypot field, single-use submission tickets, size limits, per-network and per-session quotas.
  • Show-again rules: hide the bar for 0-365 days (default 30) after a response or dismissal.
  • Your own button or script: [arnvisiox_visitor_intent] (label="Open Survey" sets the button text) and window.ARNVisitorIntent.open() (also show(), close(), dismiss()) open the panel on any page, even outside the display rules or after the visitor closed it.

💬 Call, Email and WhatsApp contact widget

A separate floating button lets visitors call, email or start a WhatsApp chat.

  • Actions: Call (phone link with its own label), Email (default subject and message) and WhatsApp (initial message; international number with country code), each on or off.
  • Content and placement: title, description and button label; bottom right or left; desktop, mobile or both; on pages where the bar is allowed.
  • Measured: widget opens and each channel’s clicks are counted in Visitor Analytics.

🧭 Display rules and smart triggers

  • Page scope: homepage only (default) or the entire site; with display rules off, the bar appears wherever the plugin is active.
  • Include and exclude pages: included pages limit the bar; excluded pages always hide it.
  • Post types: selected public post types only.
  • Audience: logged-in or logged-out, mobile or desktop, first-time or returning visitors.
  • Triggers: off by default (the bar appears at once); a delay (seconds), scroll depth (percent), exit intent (upward mouse movement on desktop, ignored on touch-only devices), page views or time on site.
  • Manual triggers: the shortcode button and the JavaScript API open the panel whenever you choose.

📊 Visitor Analytics and Visitor Intelligence

  • Visitor Analytics: impressions, panel opens and open rate, responses and conversion rate, contact leads, anonymous responses, dismissals and dismissal rate, widget opens and Call, Email and WhatsApp clicks, with a last-30-days chart, the intent breakdown and recent responses.
  • Visitor Intelligence: 7, 30 and 90-day periods with unique anonymous sessions, top intent and contact method, most active day and hour and contact rate, plus This Week, This Month, Last 30 and Last 90 Days summaries.
  • Breakdowns and funnel: intent by page, widget activity by channel, performance by trigger, submissions by hour, and the impression-to-response funnel with drop-off points and close reasons.
  • Long history: batched events and atomic daily counters, kept for two years. Session, trigger, funnel and contact-click details start with Visitor Intelligence tracking; stored responses are always included.

📨 Notifications, SMTP and response management

  • Email notifications: recipient and subject ({site_name} placeholder), optionally only for contact leads, with a “View response” link; sent in the background, so a slow mail server never delays visitors.
  • Delivery: wp_mail, a detected SMTP plugin, or the optional internal SMTP (host, port, SSL or TLS, user name, encrypted password, From, Reply-To, test email; 15-second timeout), never replacing your SMTP plugin.
  • Visitor Responses: intent, visitor, company, type (contact lead or anonymous), page, AI status and date; only administrators can view or delete them.
  • CSV export: spreadsheet-safe values and steady memory use, even with many thousands of responses.
  • Cleanup: automatic deletion after a chosen number of days (default 90), “Run Cleanup Now” with a confirmation, “Delete All Responses”, and a storage summary (response count, estimated database size).
  • Display cache reset: manual or every chosen number of days, so the bar returns for visitors who answered or dismissed it.
  • Limits & Proxy: responses per visitor network every 10 minutes (default 20), visitor events up to 300 requests per network every 10 minutes, daily notification email and AI analysis limits (default 200 each); responses are always saved, even at a limit.

📚 Consent-based recommendations block

  • “Visioix Recommendations” block and [arnvisiox_recommendations count="4"] shortcode: your latest published posts by default, up to 8.
  • Optional personalization: only with the visitor’s consent, interest categories are kept in the visitor’s browser for 30 days; no frontend AI, no account identity or browsing history.
  • Visitor control: allow personalization, or turn it off and clear preferences; logged-in users see the general list; Global Privacy Control turns it off.
  • Consent managers: window.arnvisioxGrowthConsent(true) or (false) passes the decision; withdrawal clears the stored interests.

📈 Website and Growth Intelligence with Google Site Kit

Connect visitor intent with the Analytics and Search Console data Google Site Kit already brings to your site.

  • Connections: checks that Site Kit is installed, active and set up and its data readable before any report.
  • Website Intelligence: last 28 days vs. the previous 28: users, sessions, views, views per session, engagement, bounce rate, clicks, impressions, CTR and position; cached for one hour, refreshable.
  • Highlights: top pages and products, bounce and exit risk, countries, devices, channels, top queries and search pages.
  • Website diagnosis: diagnosis, interpretation and recommendation cards with evidence and confidence, a PMI (Plus, Minus, Interesting) assessment and limited-data warnings – by AI or the rule-based Visioix Engine.
  • Growth Intelligence: data health (comparability, sample support, freshness) and completed, equal-length 7, 30 and 90-day periods ending yesterday, in accessible charts with exact daily values.
  • Growth findings: sustained traffic drop alerts, verified metric findings, pages with declining search click-through rate (with an “Edit page” link) and the largest page, channel and device changes.

🤖 Optional AI insights

  • Shared AI connection: Settings → ARN Free AI, shared by ARN Free plugins: WordPress AI (Settings → Connectors, WordPress 7.0+) or your own API key for OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi (Moonshot AI), xAI Grok, Mistral or an OpenAI-compatible HTTPS endpoint, with your model, token prices, usage history and monthly limits. Keys are stored encrypted or read from wp-config.php.
  • Response Intelligence: each new response gets a background summary, topic, priority and follow-up flag from the fields you allow (see External services), with an AI processing notice in the panel. Responses are always saved first.
  • Business insights: reason, why not, recommendations, opportunities, warnings and things to improve, from aggregate visitor counts only.
  • Website diagnosis: AI interpretation of the Site Kit comparison figures.
  • AI Queue and Cost & Usage: pending, completed and failed jobs with retry; tokens, daily and monthly usage, provider and model distribution and estimated cost.

🔒 Privacy, performance and your data

  • Consent checkbox: editable label and text; a policy page (only while published and not password-protected) in a window, the same page or a new tab; optionally required. Only the acceptance status is stored, also in the CSV.
  • Data minimization: no contact fields on anonymous responses; only the device type (not the user agent), the page address without its query string and the referrer as its site address. IP addresses serve only as hashed limit keys and are not saved with responses.
  • Trusted proxies: X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, CF-Connecting-IP or True-Client-IP, read only for requests from the proxy or CDN (such as Cloudflare) addresses you list.
  • Built for every visitor: focus moves into the opened panel, Escape closes the panel, widget and policy window, reduced motion is respected, and the panel and widget work when the browser blocks site data.
  • No ARN server: updates come from WordPress.org; external services only for features you turn on (see External services).
  • You decide what stays: deactivation removes scheduled tasks and keeps your data; data is deleted only with “Delete all plugin data when the plugin is deleted” on, per site on Multisite.

⭐ Go further with ARN Smart Visioix Pro

ARN Smart Visioix Pro, the professional visitor and website intelligence edition, includes everything in Visitor Intent and adds:

  • A visual form builder: several forms, steps with a progress bar, IF and ELSE conditional fields, a Design Studio with custom CSS, preview, display rules per form and a redirect after the answer.
  • Lead scores and Cross Intelligence linking visitor intent with website data.
  • SWOT analysis and a unified AI action plan for this week, this month and next month.
  • 7-day forecasts and early warnings; custom CSV or PDF reports, also scheduled weekly or monthly.
  • A/B testing for visitor forms and website pages.
  • Integrations: CRM endpoints, Zapier, Make, webhooks, Slack, Discord and an inbound REST API.
  • Its own AI connection under Settings → ARN Center, license management, private Pro updates and priority support.

Visitor Intent stays free and works fully without a Visioix Pro license.

🔗 More from ARN Smart

Free on WordPress.org, usable alone or together:

  • ARN Smart AI-Powered Site Utilities for Elementor – Elementor widgets, header & footer builder, SEO and schema.
  • ARN Smart Image Optimizer – local WebP and AVIF image optimization.
  • ARN Smart Duplicate Post & Content Toolkit – controlled draft preparation, duplication and find and replace.
  • ARN Smart URL Manager – short links, redirects, QR codes and local analytics.

Pro editions with more power and priority support: Vendix, Visioix, WebPix, Clonex, Linkix, SiteWatch, Contix and DualFix. Explore all products at ARN Smart.

External services

The plugin works without external services. Two optional features use them:

AI insights (ARN Free AI). This plugin does not contact any ARN server. AI features are off until a site administrator turns on AI Insights in Visitor Intent > Settings and sets up a provider under Settings > ARN Free AI.

When an administrator chooses a provider and enters their own API key, the plugin sends the text needed for the requested task to that provider only, at the moment the task runs. The API key is stored encrypted in the WordPress database. No data is sent to any other provider.

Requests are sent from your server only when:

  • a visitor response is saved while AI Insights is on: the response fields allowed in the AI privacy settings (by default the selected intent and the message; name, email, LinkedIn, and company only if you enable them), processed in the background;
  • an administrator generates AI Insights: aggregate visitor statistics (counts only);
  • an administrator generates the website diagnosis: Google Analytics and Search Console comparison figures read through Site Kit, such as metrics and the names of pages, queries, countries, devices, and channels;

  • an administrator clicks “Test connection” (a fixed test prompt, no site content) or “Load models” (the provider’s model list) under Settings > ARN Free AI.

  • OpenAI: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use , https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy

  • Anthropic (Claude): https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms , https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • Google Gemini: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms , https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • DeepSeek: https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-terms-of-use.html , https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy.html
  • Moonshot AI (Kimi): https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/agreement/modeluse , https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/agreement/userprivacy
  • xAI (Grok): https://x.ai/legal/terms-of-service , https://x.ai/legal/privacy-policy
  • Mistral AI: https://legal.mistral.ai/terms , https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/privacy-policy
  • OpenAI-compatible endpoint: requests go to the address the administrator enters; that service’s own terms apply.

If WordPress AI is chosen instead, requests go through the provider connected in WordPress (Settings > Connectors) under that provider’s terms.

The bundled ARN Free AI module keeps its settings in the arn_free_ai_settings option and daily AI usage totals (no prompts, answers or keys) in the {prefix}arn_free_ai_usage database table.

Google Site Kit (Google Analytics and Search Console). Website Intelligence and Growth Intelligence do not contact Google themselves. They read reports from the Google Site Kit plugin through your site’s own REST API on the server; Site Kit connects to Google with your site’s own connection. See the Site Kit plugin and Google’s terms (https://policies.google.com/terms) and privacy policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy).

The recommendations block, the visitor panel, and the contact widget do not use external services.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add Plugin (Add New Plugin in some WordPress versions), search for ARN Smart AI-Powered Visitor Intent, then install and activate it. You can also upload the ZIP under Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin.
  2. Open Visitor Intent → Settings. The bar already appears on the homepage with sample texts; replace them on the Content and Contact Fields tabs with your own question, reasons and fields.
  3. Choose where and when the panel appears on the Display Rules and Triggers tabs, and set up Privacy & Consent, Notifications and the Contact Widget if you need them.
  4. For Website and Growth Intelligence, install and connect the Google Site Kit plugin. For AI insights, set up a provider under Settings → ARN Free AI and turn on the AI Insights tab.
  5. Review responses under Visitor Intent → Visitor Responses and the results under Visitor Analytics and Visitor Intelligence.
sections.faq:
Do I need ARN Smart Visioix Pro or a license key?

No. ARN Smart AI-Powered Visitor Intent is free, works on its own and needs no license key; updates come from WordPress.org. ARN Smart Visioix Pro is optional: when it is activated, it deactivates Visitor Intent and continues with the same responses and settings, but it uses its own AI connection under Settings → ARN Center, so the AI provider key is entered there again. The AI usage history recorded by Visitor Intent stays under Settings → ARN Free AI and is not shown in the Pro Cost & Usage screen. Visitor Intent cannot be activated while Visioix Pro is active.

Will it slow down my site?

No. The visitor script and style load only on pages where the display rules allow the bar, the recommendations script loads only where its block or shortcode is placed, visitor events are sent in batches, and Website Intelligence reports are cached for one hour.

Does it work on WordPress Multisite?

Yes. Each site of a network keeps its own settings, responses, statistics and uninstall choice, and the visitor’s browser state (closed panel, visits, recommendation consent) is kept per site. After a network activation every site is set up on its first visit, and deleting a site also deletes its Visitor Intent tables.

What happens to my data when I delete the plugin?

By default your responses, settings and analytics are kept; scheduled tasks are always removed. With “Delete all plugin data when the plugin is deleted” on (Visitor Intent → Settings → Data & Cache), the plugin’s responses (also those in the trash), tables, options and transients are removed on each site where the option is on. Sites where ARN Smart Visioix (Pro) is active are left untouched, and while Visioix Pro is installed but deactivated the shared responses and settings are kept for it. The shared ARN Free AI settings, saved API keys and usage history of those sites are removed too, but only when no other installed ARN Free plugin (active or not) still uses them.

Does it send data to external services or AI?

Only through optional features you turn on, and never to an ARN server. AI insights send data only to the AI provider you set up under Settings → ARN Free AI, and only the response fields you allow; Website and Growth Intelligence read Google Analytics and Search Console reports from the Google Site Kit plugin on your own server. The visitor panel, the contact widget and the recommendations block use no external service. Every service is listed under External services.

How is it different from a contact form or popup plugin?

It asks for the reason of the visit first. Visitors pick why they came in one click and leave contact details only if they want, so you learn the intent of anonymous visitors as well as your leads, and the panel opens only by your display rules and triggers.

Can I choose where and when the panel appears?

Yes. Display rules set the homepage or the whole site, included and excluded pages, post types, logged-in status, device and first-time or returning visitors. Triggers open it after a delay, a scroll depth, exit intent, a number of page views or a time on site, and the shortcode or JavaScript API open it whenever you choose.

Does it support GDPR or KVKK consent?

Yes, it provides the tools: a configurable consent checkbox, a policy page shown in a window, on the same page or in a new tab, an optional requirement before submitting, data minimization and response cleanup. Site owners remain responsible for configuring them according to their legal requirements.

What do I need for Website and Growth Intelligence?

The Google Site Kit plugin, installed and connected to Google Analytics and Search Console. Visitor Intent reads the data from Site Kit on your own site; it does not contact Google itself.

My site is behind Cloudflare or another proxy. Which visitor address is used?

By default the direct connection (REMOTE_ADDR), which behind a proxy is the proxy’s address, so all visitors share one response limit. Under Visitor Intent → Settings → Limits & Proxy, choose “Behind a proxy or CDN”, the header your proxy sets, and the proxy’s IP addresses or CIDR ranges. The header is read only for requests that come from those addresses.
sections.changelog:
2.1.3

  • Fixed: The CSV export keeps a steady memory use and completes with many thousands of responses.
  • Fixed: Expired visitor limit records are cleaned up completely every hour instead of at most 1,000 an hour.
  • Fixed: On a multisite network the visitor’s browser state (closed panel, visits, recommendation consent) is kept per site.
  • Fixed: The visitor panel and the contact widget work when the browser blocks site data.
  • Fixed: The [arnvisiox_visitor_intent] button and window.ARNVisitorIntent open the panel on any page, also outside the display rules and after the visitor closed the panel.
  • Fixed: The panel’s “Sending…” and error messages can be translated.
  • Fixed: Pages kept by a page cache no longer stop the visitor form and events after a day; signed-out visitors no longer need the page’s security token.
  • Fixed: The consent policy window shows the policy page only while it is published and not password-protected.
  • Fixed: Responses keep backslashes in names, companies and messages.
  • Fixed: The new-response e-mail is sent in the background, so a slow or unreachable mail server no longer delays the visitor; internal SMTP gives up after 15 seconds.
  • Fixed: The page of a response is stored without its query string and the referrer only as its site address; older responses are shown the same way in the list, details, CSV export and e-mail.
  • Fixed: Responses keep only the visitor’s device type, not the browser’s full user agent; stored user agents are removed on update.
  • Fixed: Internal SMTP: the saved password is removed when the server, port, user name or encryption changes.
  • Fixed: Internal SMTP: the password is stored exactly as typed.
  • Fixed: A settings form with unexpected values saves nothing and shows a notice.
  • Fixed: “Manual Reset Display Cache” resets the display cache again and no longer encrypts the saved SMTP password a second time.
  • Fixed: An internal SMTP password saved in ARN Smart Visioix keeps working after switching back to Visitor Intent.
  • Fixed: Deleting Visitor Intent while ARN Smart Visioix is installed but deactivated keeps the shared responses and settings.
  • Fixed: Activating Visitor Intent with bulk actions, WP-CLI or the REST API while ARN Smart Visioix is active is refused with a message instead of a fatal error.
  • Fixed: Deleting a site from a network also deletes its Visitor Intent tables; “Delete data on uninstall” also removes the tables of sites deleted earlier.
  • Fixed: With “Delete data on uninstall”, the ARN Free AI data is removed also on sites where ARN Smart Visioix is active.
  • Fixed: After a network activation every site is set up on its first visit, so visitor events, the daily cleanup and the display cache reset work without a visit to its dashboard.
  • Fixed: Network deactivation removes the scheduled tasks of every site.
  • Fixed: Deleting a response also deletes its queued AI analysis; analyses of responses deleted earlier are removed on update and never sent.
  • Fixed: An AI job cut off by a time limit or error is retried and no longer blocks new AI insights for the same period.
  • Fixed: An empty “Delete responses after (days)” field keeps the saved period instead of deleting every response older than one day.
  • Fixed: The automatic response cleanup keeps the retention period in every time zone.
  • Fixed: “Run Cleanup Now” deletes all old responses, also while the automatic cleanup is off.
  • Fixed: The “Last 30 Days” chart shows the site’s own days in every time zone.
  • Fixed: The “View response” link in notification e-mails works for visitor responses.
  • Fixed: “Delete All Responses” and “Run Cleanup Now” run only from their buttons with the exact confirmation, never from a link.
  • Fixed: “Delete All Responses”, the response cleanup and “Delete data on uninstall” also delete responses in the trash.
  • Fixed: Shared ARN Free AI 1.0.6: the retry message shows the real number of attempts; the screen updates after “Remove saved key” and “Clear usage history”; a key set in wp-config.php is not sent to a changed endpoint; reasoning models get no temperature setting; deleting a network site removes its usage table.

Earlier versions: changelog.txt

  • Trusted proxies: X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, CF-Connecting-IP or True-Client-IP, read only for requests from the proxy or CDN (such as Cloudflare) addresses you list.
  • Built for every visitor: focus moves into the opened panel, Escape closes the panel, widget and policy window, reduced motion is respected, and the panel and widget work when the browser blocks site data.
  • No ARN server: updates come from WordPress.org; external services only for features you turn on (see External services).
  • You decide what stays: deactivation removes scheduled tasks and keeps your data; data is deleted only with “Delete all plugin data when the plugin is deleted” on, per site on Multisite.

External services

The plugin works without external services. Two optional features use them:

AI insights (ARN Free AI). This plugin does not contact any ARN server. AI features are off until a site administrator turns on AI Insights in Visitor Intent > Settings and sets up a provider under Settings > ARN Free AI.

When an administrator chooses a provider and enters their own API key, the plugin sends the text needed for the requested task to that provider only, at the moment the task runs. The API key is stored encrypted in the WordPress database. No data is sent to any other provider.

Requests are sent from your server only when:

  • a visitor response is saved while AI Insights is on: the response fields allowed in the AI privacy settings (by default the selected intent and the message; name, email, LinkedIn, and company only if you enable them), processed in the background;
  • an administrator generates AI Insights: aggregate visitor statistics (counts only);
  • an administrator generates the website diagnosis: Google Analytics and Search Console comparison figures read through Site Kit, such as metrics and the names of pages, queries, countries, devices, and channels;

  • an administrator clicks “Test connection” (a fixed test prompt, no site content) or “Load models” (the provider’s model list) under Settings > ARN Free AI.

  • OpenAI: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use , https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy

  • Anthropic (Claude): https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms , https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • Google Gemini: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms , https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • DeepSeek: https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-terms-of-use.html , https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy.html
  • Moonshot AI (Kimi): https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/agreement/modeluse , https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/agreement/userprivacy
  • xAI (Grok): https://x.ai/legal/terms-of-service , https://x.ai/legal/privacy-policy
  • Mistral AI: https://legal.mistral.ai/terms , https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/privacy-policy
  • OpenAI-compatible endpoint: requests go to the address the administrator enters; that service’s own terms apply.

If WordPress AI is chosen instead, requests go through the provider connected in WordPress (Settings > Connectors) under that provider’s terms.

The bundled ARN Free AI module keeps its settings in the arn_free_ai_settings option and daily AI usage totals (no prompts, answers or keys) in the {prefix}arn_free_ai_usage database table.

Google Site Kit (Google Analytics and Search Console). Website Intelligence and Growth Intelligence do not contact Google themselves. They read reports from the Google Site Kit plugin through your site’s own REST API on the server; Site Kit connects to Google with your site’s own connection. See the Site Kit plugin and Google’s terms (https://policies.google.com/terms) and privacy policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy).

The recommendations block, the visitor panel, and the contact widget do not use external services.
